author_note: independent reference authored without access to the tool code
reference: Pairwise-outcome corpus for a hazard-group chemical storage compatibility matrix. Each case lists a small inventory (name, physical state, CLP/GHS hazard statement codes, optional generic group meaning, optional location) and the expected matrix cell(s) in the README vocabulary X (prohibited together) / S (segregate) / U (unknown - review SDS) / C (no modelled conflict), or a boolean property (not C / not X) where the sources establish only that a pair reacts or must be separated. Expectations come from the CLP hazard-statement texts (EUH031/EUH032/EUH014/H26x/H27x), HSE HSG71 paras 71, 73, 120, the EPA-600/2-80-076 compatibility chart as transcribed by NIH ORF and Rutgers REHS and explained in WIPP Addendum B2, and the acceptance criteria of spec 11 / 00-common (unknown never safe, no inference from product name, symmetry, non-transitivity, rule id per cell, pack version in report). Stated mapping principle: fire, explosion, toxic/flammable gas or 'do not mix' -> X; heat or innocuous gas only -> S. Four randomized inventories (seed 20260916, n = 6/12/20/30) are generated by ref.py. 'group' values are generic meanings the harness maps to the tool's nearest group; null means no group chosen.
reference_citations: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP) Annex III hazard statements, texts as reproduced on EU SAMANCTA 'H/P phrases', https://sampling-manual-customs-taxation.ec.europa.eu/health-and-safety/hazardous-substances/hazard-symbols/hp-phrases_en (H200, H220, H224-H228, H240-H242, H250, H260, H261, H270-H272, H280, H290, H314, EUH001, EUH014, EUH019, EUH031, EUH032, EUH044)
HSE HSG71 Chemical warehousing: The storage of packaged dangerous substances (2009), https://www.hse.gov.uk/pubns/priced/hsg71.pdf, paras 71, 73, 109, 116, 120 (Table 2 cells not used)

Hatayama H.K. et al., A Method for Determining the Compatibility of Hazardous Wastes, EPA-600/2-80-076, April 1980; chart as reproduced at https://orf.od.nih.gov/EnvironmentalProtection/WasteDisposal/Documents/chemical_waste_chemical_compatibility_chart.pdf and https://construction.rutgers.edu/rehs/chemical-compatibilty-chart-epa (groups 1, 2, 10, 11, 30, 33, 101, 102, 104, 107)

tools.petrov.re spec 11 Chemical Compatibility & Storage Matrix (MVP, model rules, results, QA, acceptance criteria) and spec 00-common section 0.5
Case generator and count/property evaluator: bench/chemicalstorage/ref.py (stdlib, seed 20260916)
tolerance: All checks are categorical or integer and compared exactly: the tool is a rule engine with no numerical model, so there is no physical scale to set a tolerance from. Two non-scalar forms are used in the inventory cases: 'exact-subset' (every listed pair must have the stated cell; unlisted pairs are unconstrained because no source was read for them) and 'lower-bound' (count must be at least ref). Where the sources establish only a reaction or a separation duty, the check is the boolean 'not C' rather than a guessed X/S/U.

pairs_expected_S.derivation: Each listed pair must be exactly S (acid x base family; HSG71 para 120, EPA 1 x 10 / 2 x 10).

pairs_expected_not_C.derivation: Each listed pair must not be C (single-pair cases above; unclassified partner -> acceptance criterion).

record.incompatible_pairs_at_least.derivation: record.incompatible_pairs >= number of pairs known to be X (other pairs are not constrained).

not_benchmarked: Compressed gas x acid/base/corrosive and gas x non-gas flammable (README CHEM-P-011/012): no source read states these separations.
Toxic x flammable (CHEM-P-013) and pyrophoric x any (CHEM-P-008): HSG71 paras read describe pyrophorics but do not state a separation from all others; no case.
Oxidiser x combustible non-flammable organic (CHEM-P-002): 'combustible organic' cannot be expressed from hazard codes and the group list was not seen.

Flammable x non-oxidising acid and flammable x base: the LA County fact sheet lists these families as incompatible, EPA 1 x 101 was transcribed only once (H, G); sources conflict with general practice, so no expectation is set.
Caustic x oxidiser (EPA 10 x 104 transcribed once as H, G) - not confirmed.
Exceptions with a source on an X pair: spec 11 allows an explicit exception source to override the most conservative rule; README says X is never lowered. Not benchmarked either way.
Exact outcome (X vs S vs U) for organic peroxide x acid/base and water-reactive x non-aqueous partners: only 'not C' asserted.
HSG71 Table 2 cells and TRGS 510 Tabelle 2 cells: could not be read (extraction failed / 403).
Quantity limits, jurisdiction packs, secondary-containment wording, PDF layout, localisation, permalink, pictograms: out of spec MVP or not a compatibility claim.
Maximum inventory size above 30 entries: the limit is a README property, not a spec requirement.
coverage: Covers the spec 11 headline claims: prohibited oxidiser/flammable, acid/cyanide-sulfide, acid/hypochlorite, water-reactive/aqueous pairs; segregate acid/base; must-not-be-clear pairs from HSG71 and EPA; generic-group-only entry; symmetric matrix and rule id per nontrivial cell; non-transitivity; most-conservative precedence; unknown never safe (unclassified, ambiguous H314, unrecognised code, out-of-scope explosives/H241/EUH001, missing or contradictory state, contradictory group); no inference from product name (both directions); co-location and proposed groups; exception without source; pack version and SDS pointer in report; malformed/unversioned rule-pack refusal; randomized inventories up to 30 entries.
